name: Afsharid Iran (Nader Shah)

areaKm2.note: world_1715 polygon "Safavid Empire" = about 2.52 million km2 on the sphere (Iran, the Caucasus khanates, Herat and Kandahar), the last basemap before the Afghan conquest of 1722 and the nearest to Nader's restored realm. In 1739 Nader also held Kabul and the lands west of the Indus ceded by the Mughals (high); low allows for the loose hold on the Caucasus and the Persian Gulf coast. The world_1783 Persia polygon (Zand era) postdates the empire's collapse and is not used.

population.note: Infobox: about 9 million in 1736-1747 (Axworthy 2008 p. 160) (mid); about 6 million after 1747 (Axworthy 2008 pp. 160, 167) (low). High: OWID Iran 1740 = 5.55M plus Afghanistan 1740 = 2.74M (HYDE 3.3, modern borders, https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/population) = 8.29M, plus the Caucasus khanates, rounded up to 10M.

urbanization.note: Educated guess: Isfahan was still depopulated after the Afghan siege of 1722; Tabriz, Mashhad, Shiraz, Herat and Kandahar were sizeable caravan cities.

activePersonnel.note: Paper strength (Axworthy 2007 p. 639, via the article): 1736 = 150,000 (low), 1743 = 375,000 (peak). Linear interpolation to 1739 gives about 246,000 (high, rounded to 250,000); mid 200,000 because paper strengths overstate. The Indian expedition left Persia with about 80,000 and fought at Karnal with about 55,000 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Karnal, Sarkar p. 38, Rustam Ali).

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess: tribal and provincial contingents not under arms. High: the army grew from about 200,000 in 1739 to 375,000 by 1743 (Axworthy 2007 p. 639), the pool Nader could still draw on.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess: gunners, zamburak crews, engineers and the Persian Gulf fleet; the camp servants (about a third of the 160,000-strong Karnal camp) are not counted.

mobilizationRatio.note: Peak paper strength 375,000 in 1743 (Axworthy 2007 p. 639, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_of_the_Afsharid_dynasty_of_Persia) over 9 million people (Axworthy 2008 p. 160) = 0.042 (mid); low/high +/- about a quarter.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: 1744 breakdown (Axworthy 2007 p. 644, via the article): 13,000 guard cavalry (low) and 20,000 Afshar cavalry = 33,000 regular state horse (mid). High allows for other regular Khorasani horse (20 fowj of 1,000, uncited there).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: mail, sabre, lance and firearms; well mounted.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: long-service regulars trained under a uniform system in a decade of continuous campaigning.

count.note: Most of Nader's troops were light cavalry (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_of_the_Afsharid_dynasty_of_Persia): 50,000 Afghan cavalry in 1744 (Axworthy 2007 p. 644) plus Turkmen, Uzbek, Kurdish and Lur tribal horse. Mid = active less the other roles and support (200,000 - 33,000 - 15,000 - 30,000 - 8,000 = about 114,000), rounded down.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: tribal horse with lance, sword, bow and matchlock.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: experienced tribal cavalry under Nader's discipline.

count.note: Jazayerchi, uniformed and drilled heavy musketeers: 20,000 at Karnal (Ghafouri 2008 p. 383, via the article) (high); 12,000 in 1744 (Axworthy 2007 p. 644 and Hanway, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_of_the_Afsharid_dynasty_of_Persia) (low).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: heavy-calibre jazayer muskets that broke Mughal and Ottoman cavalry charges.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: drilled volley fire; Karnal and Yeghevard.

count.note: Ordinary foot musketeers (tofangchi): 40,000 in 1744 (Axworthy 2007 p. 644 and Hanway, via the article) (high); fewer in 1739 before the 1740s expansion.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: matchlock muskets.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: provincial musketeers, less drilled than the jazayerchi.

count.note: Educated guess within sourced bounds: the field army had 18 field pieces at Samarra in 1733 (von Hammer, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_of_the_Afsharid_dynasty_of_Persia) (low); "hundreds of cannons and zamburaks" at Karnal (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Karnal) (high). The many hundreds of zamburak camel swivel guns are not counted as pieces.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: lighter and more manoeuvrable than the Mughal guns (Battle of Karnal article); siege guns cast for the sieges of Kandahar and Baghdad.

count.note: Educated guess: Nader built ships at Bushehr and bought thirty ships in India (Encyclopaedia Iranica, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afsharid_Iran), mostly in the 1740s; in 1739 the Gulf fleet was a few bought European-built ships.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: second-hand merchantmen armed as warships.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25. Evidence: no naval tradition; hired crews.

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 1.0 (best-in-era) minus. Evidence: Nader Shah beat Afghans, Ottomans and the Mughals in a decade; at Karnal 55,000 men routed a far larger Mughal army in a few hours.

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.5-0.75. Evidence: a multi-ethnic army (Persian, Afghan, Turkmen, Uzbek, Kurd) held by pay, success and harsh discipline; it broke up after Nader's murder in 1747.

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.75. Evidence: unbroken victories since 1729 and the Delhi plunder of 1739.

weapons.note: Anchor: 5 (1600, musket, field cannon) to 6. Evidence: heavy jazayer muskets, matchlocks, mobile field guns and zamburaks; no bayonet-flintlock infantry.

armor.note: Anchor: 5 (half-armour). Evidence: mail and helmets for the horse.

ships.note: Anchor: 4-5. Evidence: a few European-built ships bought for the Gulf.

fortification.note: Anchor: 5 minus. Evidence: walled cities and citadels, the siege town built before Kandahar (1737-38); no trace italienne.

logistics.note: Anchor: 5 (magazines). Evidence: camel trains and depots that carried an army from Kandahar over the Khyber to Delhi (1738-39).

communications.note: Anchor: 5 minus. Evidence: mounted couriers on the caravan roads.

isr.note: Anchor: 5. Evidence: light-cavalry screens and spies; Karnal was won by luring the Mughals out of their entrenched camp.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-maddison-project-database.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true): Iran's first value is 1820 = 877 (low side); India 1750 = 1,068 (high side). Iran after the wars of 1722-1736 likely sat at the lower end. 2011 int$.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. A war state: taxes were raised harshly to pay the army, then suspended for three years after the Delhi plunder (Axworthy 2006, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afsharid_Iran); the share of output is not documented.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: silk, carpets and crafts, damaged by two decades of war.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Qanat-irrigated oases and dry farming; the army requisitioned heavily.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the other pre-modern snapshots.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: Safavid caravan roads with caravanserais and stone causeways; mostly unpaved.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess: Bushehr (Nader's naval base) and Bandar Abbas; Caspian landings.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess: Gulf trade was carried mostly by European, Indian and Arab ships.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Cavalry-heavy armies with camel trains campaigned from Mashhad to Delhi and to Bukhara and Khiva (1740).

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: camels, horses and mules of a pastoral and caravan economy (about 10% of the population); no count found.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2: plateau ringed by mountains, walled cities and local supply; population support weakened by heavy taxation.

notes: Snapshot = February 1739, Nader Shah's realm at the Battle of Karnal. Personnel: paper strength of the standing army (Axworthy) is activePersonnel, with the role split from the 1744 breakdown and the Karnal jazayerchi count; tribal contingents not yet raised are trainedReserves; camp servants are not counted. Territory = the world_1715 Safavid Empire polygon; the Mughal lands east of the Indus taken in 1739 were returned in May 1739 and are not included; includes is empty. Weakest values: activePersonnel mid (paper figures interpolated between 1736 and 1743), artillery and navy counts, GDP per capita (no Maddison value before 1820) and the economy and logistics guesses. Doctrine archetype-gunpowder-linear follows the safavid-empire-1600 precedent.
